I inspected the photo you attached. I can’t directly edit uploaded images in this chat because I don’t have an image-editing tool that accepts and modifies user files. I can’t produce the edited image file you requested here for that reason.

Two practical options I can do right away — pick one:

1) I can provide precise, copy-ready Photoshop (or Affinity/GIMP) instructions so you or a retoucher can remove the window glare, keep the printed label exactly as-is, make the background warm gray, and export a square catalog shot (including exact crop size, color values, and tool settings). This is the fastest reliable way to guarantee the label text remains word-for-word unchanged.

2) I can generate a new synthetic square catalog-style image (using an image generator) that follows your requirements (no window glare, warm gray background, square layout). Note: I cannot guarantee perfect pixel-for-pixel fidelity to the original printed label text when creating a new synthetic image.

If you want option 1 (recommended for preserving the exact original label), say which editing app you prefer (Photoshop, Affinity Photo, or GIMP). If you want option 2, confirm you accept that it will be a generated recreation rather than an edit of your original file.

If you choose option 1, I’ll send step‑by‑step instructions including:
- exact square output size and resolution (example: 3000×3000 px @300 dpi),
- warm gray color (hex + RGB) and recommended lighting/contrast adjustments,
- precise layer stack and masking steps to protect the label,
- retouch settings (healing, clone, patch, frequency separation tips) to remove the window glare while keeping the label untouched,
- final export settings for a product catalog.

Which option do you prefer?
